messages:
IncidentBot: Alert triggered — p99 latency breach on hosted:us-west-2 (routes: /v1/chat, /v1/generate). Auto-mitigation: none.
Maria: Confirming — dashboards show p95 jumped from 120ms -> 800ms and p99 ~2.4s starting ~10:12 UTC. Streaming stalls count +580%.
Raj: I'm oncall. What's the suspected root?
Maria: Correlation with kernel rollout: infra pushed trt8-3.1.0 + flashattn v2.1 to dedicated pool last deploy window. Logs show decode kernel timeouts and pagefault spikes.
Samir: Got node logs — attaching snippet:
```
E 10:12:35 decode_worker.cpp:421 page fault while mapping kv_cache
WARN GPU kernel launch failed: cuLaunchKernel() err=700
... stacktrace ...
```
Ashley: Customer impact: several customers report chat streaming stalls, some timeouts. Top affected: acme-billing (high qps), chat-widget-prod. CS flagged 3 P1s.
Raj: Rollback plan? Can we revert kernel to trt8-3.0.9 on the affected pool?
Leo: We can rollback image tag `inference-runtime:trt8-3.0.9-flashattn-v1`. But need to drain nodes — will cause short capacity drop. Suggest targeted rollback for pools serving streaming-heavy routes.
Maria: Agreed. Also recommended temporary mitigation: force decode path to fallback to `cpu_kv_cache` and disable `continuous_batching` for streaming routes.
Raj: Commands to apply (I'll run):
```
kubectl -n inference set image ds/inference-runtime inference-runtime=inference-runtime:trt8-3.0.9-flashattn-v1
kubectl -n inference rollout restart ds/inference-runtime --selector=pool=streaming-heavy
```
Samir: Also set runtime flag to disable new compile flags:
```
kubectl -n inference create configmap runtime-flags --from-literal=DECODE_USE_NEW_KERNEL=false -o yaml --dry-run=client | kubectl apply -f -
```
Maria: I'm pushing a circuit-breaker rule in the router to failfast slow decode >1.5s to protect downstream services.
CustomerOps: Noting impacted customers, opening incident page, will send status update in 15.
DeployBot: Canary rollback to trt8-3.0.9 started for pool streaming-heavy (3/15 nodes rolled).
Raj: Monitoring p95/p99 on the canary. Maria, can you watch streaming stall counts and KV pagefault rates?
Maria: Watching. Early signs: p99 on canary nodes back to ~220ms, overall p99 starts trending down. KV pagefaults drop by ~85% on rolled nodes.
Ashley: CS — send tentative note: "We are rolling back a recent runtime kernel change to mitigate streaming stalls and reduce tail latency. Engineering is monitoring."
Samir: One caveat — some pools still on trt8-3.1.0. Need to coordinate multi-pool rollback or progressive canary.
Raj: Plan: finish targeted rollback, monitor 30m, then decide global rollback. I'll create a follow-up incident thread after 30m.
IncidentBot: Incident acknowledged by Raj. Severity: Sev2. Start time: 3412345678.
Maria: Recording postmortem items: test matrix for flashattn v2 on long sequence streaming, add perf regression gating for compile flags, and improve canary traffic split for decode-heavy endpoints.
Raj: Handoff to eng-runtime for next shift: please continue monitoring, escalate if p99 >1s.
Leo: Adding owner tag `eng-runtime` to incident.
CustomerOps: Posted customer update v1 at 10:29 UTC.
Maria: Will prepare list of affected tokens and traces for SLO/regression alerts.
Samir: Noted — capturing core dumps from one failed node, uploading to shared storage.
Raj: Thanks team. I'll update after the 30m observation window.
